title: Public Sector Superannuation Legislation Amendment Bill 2018
short_title: Public Sector Superannuation Legislation Amendment Bill 2018

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would revise public sector superannuation arrangements for parliamentarians, members of the Judges' Pensions Scheme and eligible children, and reduce the trustee corporation's board.
It would correct parliamentary lump sum safety-net calculations, allow eligible scheme members to release money for Division 293 tax, and standardise children's benefit eligibility.
The Commonwealth Superannuation Corporation board would reduce from 11 to nine directors from 1 July 2020, with earlier appointments preserved under transitional arrangements.
changes: The age from which eligible children had to study full time would rise from 16 to 18.
Employment restrictions affecting children's eligibility would be removed where applicable under the relevant schemes.
The Parliamentary Retiring Allowances Trust could pass resolutions without meetings after setting procedures and informing, or attempting to inform, all trustees.
Release authority lump sums from the Judges' Pensions Scheme could not reduce a member's retirement pension below zero.
summary.affected: Covered parliamentarians and their estates, eligible Judges' Pensions Scheme members, children of deceased scheme members, trustees and Commonwealth Superannuation Corporation directors would be affected.

speeches.speaker: David Coleman
speeches.brief: The Public Sector Superannuation Legislation Amendment Bill 2018 makes four key changes: allowing non-judge members of the Judges' Pensions Scheme to request a lump sum for the division 293 tax; fixing the calculation of lump sum superannuation guarantee safety net benefits for estates under the Parliamentary Contributory Superannuation Act; raising the minimum age for child reversionary benefits from 16 to 18 and removing the employment condition; and reducing the Commonwealth Superannuation Corporation board from 11 to nine directors.

speeches.speaker: Jim Chalmers
speeches.brief: Labor supported the Public Sector Superannuation Legislation Amendment Bill 2018 for its technical changes to superannuation for public servants, judges and parliamentarians, but criticised the government for failing to address unpaid superannuation for the broader workforce, where 2.4 million workers lose $5.6 billion annually, and for proposing an amnesty that would let employers avoid penalties for unpaid super.

speeches.speaker: David Coleman
speeches.brief: The Public Sector Superannuation Legislation Amendment Bill 2018 makes four key changes: allowing non-judge members of the Judges' Pensions Scheme to release lump sums for division 293 tax, fixing the superannuation guarantee safety net calculation for parliamentary pensions, changing child reversionary benefit eligibility from age 16 to 18 and removing the employment test, and reducing the Commonwealth Superannuation Corporation Board from 11 to nine directors. It also includes minor amendments to the Parliamentary Contributory Superannuation Act, such as allowing trust resolutions without a meeting and permitting actuaries other than the Australian Government Actuary to provide advice.
